panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient showing tongue atrophy with visible fasciculation, explicitly captioned as occurring at the time of diagnosis of spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA). The in-text mention confirms bulbar paralysis with atrophy and fasciculation of the tongue in a 70-year-old patient, a classic bulbar manifestation of SBMA (Kennedy disease). Fasciculation is noted from the image/caption but has no dedicated vocabulary key, so it is listed as a proposed finding.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of an open mouth showing a furrowed, atrophic tongue with rightward uvula deviation. The article title identifies X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (Kennedy's disease) and the caption/in-text attribute the findings to bulbar compromise ('tongue atrophy with fasciculations', 'deviation of the uvula to right'), a classic bulbar manifestation of SBMA. The uvula deviation is an additional captioned bulbar sign absent from the vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding. No ethnicity or age is stated in the caption or in-text.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E muscle biopsy from a genetically defined SBMA patient showing rimmed vacuoles and myofibrillar aggregates; caption explicitly attributes to SBMA. B: Higher-magnification H&E of the same SBMA biopsy with rimmed vacuoles and cytoplasmic body aggregate. C: Panel C of the SBMA biopsy showing core-lobulated fibers with myofibrillar aggregates. D: Myotilin immunohistochemistry of SBMA biopsy showing strongly immunoreactive myofibrillar aggregates.
panels.attribution_text: Jokela et al. Distinct Muscle Biopsy Findings in Genetically Defined Adult-Onset Motor Neuron Disorders.. PloS one 2016. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0151376. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Secondary “myopathic” changes in SBMA. Muscle biopsy from a vastus lateralis biopsy of a 46-year-old male patient with SBMA showing internal nuclei, rimmed vacuoles (RV, yellow arrows, A-B), one RV and”cytoplasmic body” aggregate (green arrow), core-lobulated fibers with myofibrillar aggregates (black arrows in A-B, yellow arrows in C) that are strongly myotilin immunoreactive (yellow arrows, D).
in_text_mentions: hology, we performed further immunohistological evaluations for Z-disc components (myotilin, desmin, alphaB-crystallin, BAG3), dystrophin carboxy terminal (DYS-2) and autophagy markers (LC3b, VCP, TDP-43, SMI-31, p62). The results are shown in Table 3 and Figs 2 and 3. The myofibrillar lesions were strongly myotilin and alphaB-crystallin immunopositive and ectopic dystrophin expression was usually present in the same fiber regions. In the rimmed vacuolated fibers protein aggregates were immunoreactive for markers of autophagic processing, including ubiquitin, p62, SMI-31, TDP-43, VCP and LC3b.
